stories.title: Eddie Kingston Double Champion and Continental Cup
stories.tldr: Eddie Kingston made his triumphant return to AEW television after more than six months away, defeating Jake Doyle in the opening round of the inaugural Continental Challenge Cup tournament. Kingston, who requested to be included in the tournament, dedicated his entire run to the fans who supported him during his absence and inspired him to keep fighting. The Mad King advanced to the quarterfinals where he will face a blind draw opponent, with the tournament final taking place at All In.

stories.title: Chris Jericho New Opportunity in AEW
stories.tldr: Chris Jericho has earned a TNT Championship opportunity against Kevin Knight at AEW Dynamite on August 12, a title he has never won in AEW despite holding nearly every other championship. The match was set up after Jericho assisted Darby Allin at Grand Slam Mexico, though Knight is heavily favored to retain before facing Allin in a Falls Count Anywhere match at All In. Jericho remains committed to active competition with no retirement timeline, stating he will continue wrestling as long as he feels creatively fulfilled and can deliver quality matches.

stories.title: AEW Referee Aubrey Edwards and Match Stipulations
stories.tldr: AEW Referee Aubrey Edwards, the first female referee to call a main event match on both TV and PPV, revealed that Blood and Guts is the hardest match stipulation to prepare for due to the dual-ring cage setup, difficulty communicating time cues from a distance, and an unexpected challenge: the overwhelming iron-like smell of blood.

stories.title: Hurt Syndicate Business Offer in AEW
stories.tldr: After six weeks without receiving a single offer since opening for business, the Hurt Syndicate finally got their first client when Shane Taylor Promotions approached them with an envelope full of cash on AEW Collision. The proposal's exact purpose remains unclear, but it could involve helping STP challenge for the AEW trios titles or securing a world title shot through the Casino Gauntlet at All In.

stories.title: Tweets of the Week Jon Moxley and Renee
stories.tldr: Wrestling's social media landscape delivered plenty of laughs this week as Jon Moxley surprised Renee Paquette with an ice bucket challenge for ALS awareness, while other wrestlers like Danhausen, Steve Austin, and Dalton Castle entertained fans with humorous posts and videos. The collection showcased everything from NWA's recruitment humor to behind-the-scenes antics and creative editing from various wrestling personalities across multiple promotions.

stories.title: AEW MyAEW Streaming Platform Investment
stories.tldr: AEW is planning a significant investment in its MyAEW streaming platform to address what fans have criticized as a lackluster service. The company has been expanding the platform by adding shows from multiple promotions including RevPro and Pro Wrestling EVE, and plans constant updates and improvements. AEW views the platform as crucial to its business strategy and sees an opportunity following the failure of competing streaming services like TrillerTV.

stories.title: Andrade El Idolo Injury
stories.tldr: Andrade El Idolo announced he will be out of action for a few days to several weeks following AEW Grand Slam Mexico, though he emphasized the injury is not serious. He worked two additional MLP Canada shows before seeking medical attention in Miami. MJF responded by mocking Andrade's injury on social media, using El Idolo's own catchphrase against him and taking credit for the attack that occurred at Grand Slam.

stories.title: Jim Ross AEW Broadcasting Career
stories.tldr: Jim Ross discussed his vision for ending his broadcasting career on his podcast, emphasizing he wants a planned departure rather than an abrupt exit. The 74-year-old doesn't want to be finished but would accept if AEW declines to renew his contract, prioritizing advance notice and a deliberate closing moment. He confirmed his brain surgery is scheduled for August 12 and expressed hope of returning for AEW All In: London on August 30.

stories.title: AEW Grand Slam Mexico Viewership
stories.tldr: AEW Grand Slam Mexico posted strong viewership numbers on TBS with 694,000 viewers and a 0.14 demo rating, both increases from the previous week's Dynamite broadcast. The event's most-viewed YouTube clips were led by MJF's Triple B segment, followed by Místico's Arena México entrance and several high-profile matches from the card.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite Viewership August 5
stories.tldr: AEW Dynamite's August 5 episode drew 694,000 viewers with a 0.16 key demo rating, up from the previous week but down compared to the same date last year. The viewership increase of 18,000 viewers week-to-week represents a modest recovery for the program on TBS.

stories.title: AEW Continental Cup 2026
stories.tldr: Six wrestlers have emerged as potential favorites to win the 2026 Continental Cup at AEW All In, with Jon Moxley looking to add the tournament victory to his current Continental Championship reign. The field includes technical specialists like Roderick Strong and David Finlay, returning wrestler Jay White, surprising contender Orange Cassidy, and UK native Nigel McGuinness, who could make history competing in his home country.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite and Collision Matches August 12-15
stories.tldr: Kevin Knight will defend his TNT Championship against Chris Jericho on August 12 Dynamite in Las Vegas. Darby Allin challenged Knight to a Falls Count Anywhere match at AEW All In: London on August 30. Three more Continental Challenge Cup first-round matches were announced for the August 15 Collision episode.

stories.title: WWE Star Commentary and Interviews
stories.tldr: Multiple WWE Superstars have made headlines through recent interviews, with Je'Von Evans and Chad Gable discussing dream entrance music, Dragon Lee outlining championship ambitions with Rey Mysterio, and The Undertaker reflecting on his greatest WrestleMania moments. Additionally, Chelsea Green's interim Women's Championship victory has sparked discussions about opportunities for newer talent, while several veterans like AJ Styles and Matt Hardy have commented on the state of the roster.

stories.title: The Miz Discusses Criticism and New Trademark
stories.tldr: The Miz has revealed that criticism has fueled his 20-year wrestling career, stating he thrives on negativity and views himself as an underdog. Meanwhile, WWE has filed a trademark application for "The Mike" on August 7, 2026, apparently as a playful response to a running gag on The Pat McAfee Show involving baseball pitcher Jacob Misiorowski, who shares The Miz nickname.

stories.title: Blake Monroe WWE Presentation Changes
stories.tldr: Blake Monroe, who hasn't yet wrestled a televised main roster match in WWE despite attacking Giulia on SmackDown in June, has teased that her entrance presentation will change ahead of her official in-ring debut. Monroe praised Triple H for being hands-on and noted his expertise with entrances, while also reflecting on her previous matches against Giulia in Japan, saying she has grown significantly as a wrestler since their 2023 encounter.

stories.title: Jimmy Hart WWE Hall of Famer Comments
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Jimmy Hart maintains that Hulk Hogan was booed at WWE's January 2025 Netflix debut in Los Angeles due to political divisions rather than past controversies, noting they received cheers the following night in Texas. Hart also discussed The Gentry's upcoming album "It's Been So Long," featuring previously unreleased recordings from 56 years ago discovered in the Sun Records vault.

stories.title: Elijah Holyfield Sent to AAA
stories.tldr: Elijah Holyfield has been reassigned from NXT to AAA after Shawn Michaels announced the move on WWE LFG. The 28-year-old, who transitioned from football to professional wrestling in December 2024, will now train under The Undertaker in a different wrestling environment. WWE appears to be testing Holyfield's potential by moving him outside the typical developmental bubble after less than two years in the business.

stories.title: WWE SmackDown Recap and Continental Cup
stories.tldr: The Bryan & Vinny Show discussed WWE SmackDown which featured two standout promos but suffered from a weak main event, while also covering the Continental Cup Collision matches which were the first installment of what appears to be a predictable tournament series.

stories.title: Brock Lesnar vs Kurt Angle WWE Matches
stories.tldr: WWE Vault has compiled a video featuring every match between Brock Lesnar and Kurt Angle during their time in WWE. The two competitors engaged in an intense physical rivalry that included several high-stakes championship encounters. This collection showcases the technical wrestling and athleticism that defined their matchups in the company.

stories.title: John Cena vs Randy Orton WWE Title Matches
stories.tldr: A comprehensive video compilation documents the entire WWE Championship rivalry between John Cena and Randy Orton, spanning from their first encounter at SummerSlam 2007 to their final match at Backlash 2025. The five-hour retrospective showcases their epic battles across multiple stipulations including Iron Man matches, Hell in a Cell, and Ladder matches, capturing the physical and psychological evolution of one of wrestling's most iconic rivalries.

stories.title: Ric Flair Personal Life Update
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair and Wendy Barlow have reconciled once again as of August 2026. The couple, who married in 2018 after meeting in WCW years prior, have had an on-and-off relationship, splitting in 2022 and again in 2024 before getting back together. Flair announced their reunion via Twitter/X with his characteristically boastful tone.

stories.title: Mickie James Names Dream Opponents for Nick Aldis
stories.tldr: Mickie James recently discussed three potential future opponents for her husband Nick Aldis in WWE, including Randy Orton, Cody Rhodes, and Drew McIntyre. James expressed her desire to see these matches happen, highlighting the existing storylines and history between Aldis and each of these competitors. Aldis has already faced GUNTHER at SummerSlam in his WWE in-ring debut after working as SmackDown General Manager.

stories.title: WWE Television Rule and Match Idea
stories.tldr: During an August 9, 2026 episode of WWE programming, Kevin Owens shut down Harlem Lewis's pitch to spit on his opponent as a heel tactic, revealing that WWE has a television-specific rule prohibiting spitting during matches. Owens explained the restriction wasn't about whether the spot would draw heat, but rather that the company has a hard rule against allowing that kind of content on TV.

stories.title: Kevin Owens NBA Sneaker Appearance
stories.tldr: Kevin Owens wore Ja Morant's signature "Explorer" Jurassic Park x Nike Ja 3 sneakers during his August 7 WWE SmackDown appearance, where he continued building toward a title match against CM Punk. The Memphis Grizzlies star noticed the footwear choice and responded with approval on social media, showing appreciation for Owens' fashion statement.

stories.title: Former WWE Star EC3 Social Media Commentary
stories.tldr: Triple H and Stephanie McMahon's 15-year-old daughter performed the national anthem at WWE SummerSlam 2026, but faced online criticism despite delivering a strong performance. Former WWE star EC3 criticized fans on social media for attacking an innocent teenager, arguing that such behavior invalidates their opinions about wrestling creative and damages their credibility with company leadership.

stories.title: Je'Von Evans Randy Orton Record and World Title
stories.tldr: WWE's Je'Von Evans discussed his ambitions to break Randy Orton's record and revealed which World Title he would bring back if he becomes WWE Champion. Evans expressed his desire to use "Big Goldie" (the original WWE Championship design) if he achieves his goal, while also sharing his ideal entrance music choices and his thoughts on Grayson Waller's recent criticism of the NXT men's roster.

stories.title: WWE SmackDown August 7 Report
stories.tldr: Bryan Alvarez provided his detailed coverage of WWE SmackDown from August 7, 2026. The report is available exclusively for subscribers on the Wrestling Observer Newsletter. However, the full details of what transpired on the show are not included in this excerpt.

stories.title: Lexis King and AJ Styles Son Avery Drama
stories.tldr: The Avery Styles controversy has expanded beyond the initial GCW incident, with major wrestlers and promotions now weighing in on the "pay your dues" debate. NGW Tennessee publicly defended Avery as professional and helpful, while Lexis King and A.J. Francis argued that sons of legends are treated differently on the indie circuit, and BJ Ray called the entire "pay your dues" mentality insecure and childish.

stories.title: Brock Lesnar Final WWE Match Emotional Atmosphere
stories.tldr: Following Lesnar's retirement announcement, new details have emerged about the emotional backstage moments surrounding his final match, including Oba Femi's respectful post-match visit to Lesnar's locker room. WWE leadership and fellow wrestlers have reflected on Lesnar's legacy, while speculation grows about his potential WWE Hall of Fame induction next year in Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: John Cena Retirement and Contract Status
stories.tldr: Cena remains under a multi-year WWE ambassador contract that contractually prevents him from wrestling elsewhere, effectively blocking any potential AEW offer. WWE is targeting December for the previously announced John Cena Classic tournament. While Cena has softened his absolute retirement stance by saying it would take "financial suicide" to lure him back, the contractual restrictions make an outside promotion signing him nearly impossible.

stories.title: Chelsea Green Championship Interim and AAA
stories.tldr: Following her interim WWE Women's Championship victory at SummerSlam, Chelsea Green has already requested permission to bring the title to AAA for a potential defense. Green previously held the AAA World Mixed Tag Team Championship with Ethan Page before losing it due to her orbital fracture injury. The request has not yet been approved by either WWE or AAA, and no match has been announced.

stories.title: Brock Rechsteiner NFL and WWE Interest
stories.tldr: WWE's interest in Brock Rechsteiner remains unshaken despite his six-game NFL suspension, with company officials confident it won't affect their plans to sign him. Rechsteiner has reportedly expressed his own interest in joining WWE, and the company has been monitoring him since his college days. He joined WWE's NIL program in 2025 after Triple H offered him a deal.

stories.title: Matt Cardona WWE Entrance Theme
stories.tldr: Matt Cardona elaborated on his desire to use "When the Lights Go Down" by Downstait for his WWE return, explaining how the band reunited specifically to create the song for him after his initial release. He also credited his 2019 death match with Nick Gage as the pivotal moment that ultimately led to his WWE comeback, and revealed WWE is now allowing him more personal freedom, including appearing on the latest season of WWE: Unreal.

stories.title: Dominik Mysterio AAA and WWE Booking
stories.tldr: Dominik Mysterio has now formally called for greater consistency in his character portrayal across WWE and AAA, arguing his serious AAA Mega Champion status should be reflected in his WWE booking. After losing the "Human Monies" feud to Danhausen at SummerSlam, Mysterio is preparing to defend his AAA title at TripleMania 34 next month.

stories.title: El Grande Americano World Heavyweight Championship Tournament Correction
stories.tldr: Dave Meltzer has corrected the previous report that El Grande Americano would win the tournament and challenge Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship. WWE's official eight-man bracket confirms Americano is not included in the field. The tournament will proceed as originally scheduled with eight confirmed competitors across four first-round matches.

stories.title: Alex Wright WCW and WWE History
stories.tldr: Alex Wright moved to the U.S. for WCW at 18 but went roughly half a year without pay, living in airport hotels while accumulating debt. After confronting Eric Bischoff directly, he finally received payment and eventually became a television regular, though he initially resisted his signature dancing gimmick. Wright later turned down WWE twice after WCW closed, including a proposed program with Hulk Hogan, citing physical and mental burnout from his WCW run.

stories.title: Mason Rook vs Kam Hendrix Social Media Feud
stories.tldr: Mason Rook and Kam Hendrix have escalated their social media feud on Twitter, with Rook firing back at Hendrix's AI-generated car image by posting a "cuck chair" meme that references Hendrix's real-life wife Maxxine Dupri being involved in a romantic storyline with Austin Theory on WWE programming. This marks the second round of their Twitter war in eight days, following an earlier exchange involving jokes about fried chicken and Hendrix's personal life.

stories.title: Kevin Nash Political Commentary
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer and Army veteran Kevin Nash launched a fierce political attack on Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth via Twitter, declaring that America has lost the war in the Middle East and comparing them to drivers of a "clown car." Nash engaged in multiple heated exchanges with critics throughout the day, bringing up geopolitical concerns ranging from Ukraine to Iran's nuclear capabilities while predicting a Democratic electoral victory.

stories.title: WCW Historical Retrospective
stories.tldr: Wrestling Observer Live's Josh Nason discussed AEW's recent programming including the Continental Challenge Cup tournament, addressed an AJ Styles versus Arik Cannon social media dispute over paying dues, and highlighted his main topic about the wrestling industry's reluctance to publicly celebrate major accomplishments like stadium attendance figures due to year-over-year comparisons being unfavorable.

stories.title: Paige Collett Personal Story
stories.tldr: Professional wrestler Paige Collett shared details about a recent hookup in which the man mistakenly believed she was 19 years old and subsequently ghosted her. Collett opened up about the encounter to illustrate that people living with chronic pain conditions like CRPS can still experience normal intimacy and adventure. The experience came after years of being unable to tolerate physical contact due to her condition, and she emphasized that her openness is meant to inspire others with chronic illnesses to continue living full lives.

stories.title: Jim Ross Mourns Dory Funk Jr
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Jim Ross paid tribute to the late Dory Funk Jr., who passed away on August 4 at age 85. Ross shared memories of working with Funk during his early career and praised his exceptional abilities as a trainer who helped develop stars like Kurt Angle, Edge, and Christian Cage.

stories.title: TNA Ring Comparison with Gail Kim
stories.tldr: Former TNA Knockouts Champion Gail Kim recently compared the promotion's iconic six-sided ring to the traditional four-sided WWE-style ring during an interview. While Kim appreciated the unique aesthetic and concept of the six-sided ring, she acknowledged that it was physically harder on wrestlers' bodies and preferred the standard four-sided ring for in-ring performance, though she noted the six-sided ring offered better stability at the turnbuckles.

stories.title: Dave Bautista God of War Acting Role
stories.tldr: Dave Bautista is reportedly in negotiations to play Kratos in Prime Video's upcoming God of War series, though a deal has not yet been finalized. The former WWE Champion would be stepping into a role previously held by Ryan Hurst, who suffered a torn biceps that delayed his availability until 2027. The adaptation will draw from recent God of War games and has already been ordered for two seasons, with production aiming to resume later this year.

stories.title: AAA News Verano de Escándalo
stories.tldr: AAA's Verano de Escándalo event concluded with several major announcements including Liv Morgan's appearance, a mystery attacker unmasking Psycho Clown, and the completion of the Triplemanía 34 card. Key developments included El Fiscal earning a Latin American Championship match, Damián 666 joining Perros del Mal, and Ricky Saints challenging Rey Fenix for the Cruiserweight Championship.

stories.title: Tetsuya Naito NOAH GHC Championship
stories.tldr: Tetsuya Naito captured the GHC Heavyweight Championship on August 9, 2026, defeating Shane Haste at Korakuen Hall in Tokyo. The victory marks a significant addition to Naito's already decorated resume and establishes him as the 51st GHC champion. Notably, Naito announced he will skip the upcoming N-1 tournament and instead focus on defending his new NOAH title.

stories.title: Adam Copeland Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling Match
stories.tldr: Adam Copeland is set to compete against former TNA World Champion Steve Maclin at Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling's Northern Rising event on October 3rd in Toronto, Ontario. The match will take place at Maple Leaf Gardens, also known as the Mattany Athletic Centre, as one of the pay-per-view's main events. Maclin recently departed from TNA Wrestling after receiving his release in June.

stories.title: La Catalina AAA to WWE Performance Center
stories.tldr: La Catalina, a Lucha Libre AAA star, is reportedly expected to visit the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Florida next week. The Mexican wrestler recently transitioned from CMLL to AAA in April and has been competing in high-profile matches, though it remains unclear whether this visit will lead to NXT programming appearances.

stories.title: WWE star Thea Hail’s “Happy Sunday” bikini photo shoot
stories.tldr: WWE NXT star Thea Hail shared beach photos on Instagram over the weekend, trading her wrestling gear for a bikini while posing with ocean and sand dunes in the background. The post, captioned "Happy Sunday," received supportive comments from fellow WWE stars Ivy Nile and Kiana James, who responded with enthusiastic emojis and encouragement.

stories.title: Rumor Look Back: Feb. 2 – 8, 2026
stories.tldr: A retrospective look at wrestling rumors from February 2-4, 2026, examining how predictions about major storylines and wrestler movements played out over the following six months. Key stories included Chris Jericho's AEW contract status, injuries to Brie Bella and other WWE talent, WrestleMania 42 main event plans, and the departures of Ava, Tommaso Ciampa, and AJ Styles from WWE. Most rumors proved accurate, though some WrestleMania matches changed and AEW failed to capitalize on signing AJ Styles after his WWE retirement.

stories.title: MVP Teases Wrestling Retirement
stories.tldr: MVP has accelerated his retirement timeline, now saying his final match could come as early as next year rather than 2027. The 52-year-old emphasized he no longer has the explosiveness or desire for singles competition, though he remains willing to work tag team and trios matches for AEW. He also stated he would decline an AEW Championship opportunity on his way out.

stories.title: WWE and AEW Speculation on Free Agent Steve Maclin
stories.tldr: Maclin made an immediate impact at Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling's August 7 tapings, defeating Psycho Mike before attacking both Rhino and multiple officials in a chaotic segment that escalated into a con-chair-to. The angle sets up a potential program at the promotion's Northern Rising event, where Adam Copeland is already scheduled. AEW has had preliminary contact with Maclin since his TNA departure, though no deal has been confirmed, and WWE speculation continues.

stories.title: Current WWE Champion Set For Upcoming Match In Another Promotion
stories.tldr: Baron Corbin will defend the MLW World Tag Team Championship as Bishop Dyer alongside Donovan Dijak against the Good Brothers on next week's MLW Fusion, in what appears to be his final match for the promotion before focusing on his WWE run. The match was taped prior to his WWE return. With Corbin back in WWE and holding the US Championship, there's speculation about a potential reunion with former NXT tag partner Bron Breakker on the main roster.

stories.title: Darby Allin TNT Championship matches at AEW events
stories.tldr: Kevin Knight is scheduled to defend the TNT Championship against Chris Jericho on August 12 AEW Dynamite after issuing a challenge during AEW Collision. This match comes after Darby Allin challenged Knight to a Falls Count Anywhere match at AEW All In, but Knight opted to address Jericho first, citing Jericho's involvement in Allin's recent victory over him at Grand Slam Mexico. The winner of the Jericho match will then potentially face Allin at All In.

stories.title: AEW Continental Challenge Cup tournament
stories.tldr: AEW has officially revealed the Continental Challenge Cup tournament format, a 16-wrestler knockout competition featuring blind draw matches with no time limits or outside interference allowed. The tournament culminates at AEW All In London on August 30 at Wembley Stadium, where the winner will become the new AEW Continental Champion. Three additional first-round matches have been set for the August 15 episode of Collision.

stories.title: Chris Jericho AEW contract renewal
stories.tldr: Chris Jericho has renewed his AEW contract and revealed he considered other options, including a potential WWE return, before deciding to stay with the company he helped create. While Jericho weighed his options, his ownership stake in AEW and emotional investment in the promotion's growth ultimately led him to re-sign rather than explore opportunities elsewhere.

stories.title: Toni Storm mystery attacker in AEW
stories.tldr: Toni Storm remains absent from AEW programming after being attacked by an unknown assailant backstage during a March episode of Dynamite. Tony Schiavone and Luther recently speculated on the identity of the attacker, with Schiavone naming Thekla and Mercedes Mone as suspects while Luther suggested everyone in the women's locker room could be responsible due to jealousy of Storm.

stories.title: AEW All In London 2026 returns
stories.tldr: With AEW All In London 2026 just over three weeks away at Wembley Stadium on August 30, the pay-per-view is expected to feature eight notable returns that could reshape the promotion's roster. From injured stars like Buddy Matthews and Keith Lee to those taking time away like Ruby Soho and Dr Britt Baker DMD, these comebacks could prove pivotal for various wrestlers and factions heading into the event.

stories.title: Nyla Rose AEW behind-the-scenes work
stories.tldr: Nyla Rose, a former AEW Women's World Champion, revealed during a virtual signing that she has been working behind-the-scenes for AEW since her last televised match in November 2024 on Rampage. Beyond her backstage duties, Rose has also been active on the independent wrestling circuit and toured extensively throughout Japan with her tag team partner Nightshade. During the Q&A, Rose also shared that she once pitched a tag team concept with Yuka Sakazaki called "The Magical Beasts."

stories.title: AEW Brawling Birds tag team
stories.tldr: AEW's Brawling Birds, comprised of Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor, have become a dominant tag team in recent months. The pairing came together in January when a producer approached Windsor about teaming with Hayter, and the duo quickly learned their team name came from Tony Khan, who appreciated its British reference. While still chasing gold, the Brawling Birds have set their sights on defeating Divine Dominion for the AEW Women's Tag Team Championships, potentially at AEW All In in England.

stories.title: AEW Death Riders group chat
stories.tldr: Claudio Castagnoli revealed that the Death Riders group chat is used primarily for sharing wrestling videos, training techniques, and inspirational content to keep members motivated. The AEW star also confirmed he's part of a coffee-themed group chat with WWE's Seth Rollins and John Cena, where the trio exchange recommendations about different coffee shops they visit.

stories.title: Paige WWE SmackDown return
stories.tldr: Paige is returning to WWE SmackDown on August 14 in Boston following her attack by The Bella Twins at SummerSlam. Nikki Bella blamed Paige for costing them the Women's Tag Team Championships and vowed to make her life miserable, but Paige fired back on social media claiming she actually won those championships and saved Nikki from being pinned. The confrontation is set to unfold on next week's SmackDown, which also features three championship matches.

stories.title: WWE GUNTHER Danhausen curse
stories.tldr: WWE's GUNTHER has publicly dismissed Danhausen's curses as nothing more than fantasy, comparing them to belief in Santa Claus ahead of SummerSlam 2026. Meanwhile, Danhausen has been expanding his curse portfolio beyond sports teams to include celebrities like Tom Brady, Drake, and Conor McGregor, claiming credit for McGregor's recent injury during his UFC comeback.

stories.title: Undertaker and Mick Foley Hell in a Cell history
stories.tldr: In a recent interview, WWE's Undertaker recalled his legendary 1998 Hell in a Cell match against Mick Foley, revealing that he genuinely feared Foley may have died after his infamous falls from the top of the cage and through its middle. Undertaker expressed respect for Foley's willingness to risk his body to deliver an unforgettable match, while noting that the falls looked far worse from his vantage point on top of the cell. The two wrestlers now work on opposite sides of the wrestling business, with Undertaker serving as a creative ambassador for WWE's AAA and Foley as an interviewer for AEW.

stories.title: Triple H WWE live events debate
stories.tldr: Triple H recently discussed the ongoing internal debate in WWE about the appropriate number of live events for talent to work. He acknowledged the challenge of balancing the developmental benefits of house shows against the physical toll of constant touring, while emphasizing that live events remain important and shouldn't be eliminated entirely.

stories.title: Matt Cardona WWE return reflection
stories.tldr: Matt Cardona credits his July 2021 Death Match victory over Nick Gage for the GCW World Championship as the pivotal moment that led to his WWE return in January 2026. The brutal independent bout, which left him severely injured, helped him reinvent his character beyond his previous "Zack Ryder" PG persona and ultimately proved instrumental in getting him back to WWE. Cardona has revealed he wanted to keep his independent entrance music upon his return but was not permitted to do so.

stories.title: WWE star entrance music restrictions
stories.tldr: Matt Cardona wanted to use his independent entrance music "When The Lights Go Down" by Downstait when he returned to WWE in January 2026, but WWE management did not permit it. The song was specially created for Cardona by Downstait after his initial WWE release and has significant sentimental value to him. This stands in contrast to Cody Rhodes, who was allowed to keep his Downstait entrance theme "Kingdom" when he returned to the company at WrestleMania 38.

stories.title: Dominik Mysterio Eddie Guerrero custody feud reflection
stories.tldr: Dominik Mysterio recently reflected on his involvement in the famous 2005 custody storyline between Rey Mysterio and Eddie Guerrero when he was just eight years old. Despite being nervous about appearing on camera, Dominik agreed to participate partly to avoid school, and he recalls the support he received from WWE staff and the wrestlers involved after his segments. The experience ultimately sparked his passion for wrestling, though it caused confusion at his school where teachers believed the storyline was real.

stories.title: Blake Monroe dating wrestlers advice
stories.tldr: WWE star Blake Monroe advised against dating wrestlers during a TMZ interview, citing the challenges of the profession's demanding travel schedule and inherent jealousy issues. Monroe explained that wrestlers understand each other's unique lifestyle, but the provocative nature of the business and constant road time make relationships between performers particularly difficult.

stories.title: Dragon Lee and AJ Styles tag team
stories.tldr: Dragon Lee recently reflected on his tag team with AJ Styles, which captured the World Tag Team Championship on WWE Raw before Styles' retirement. Lee credited Styles with pushing him to the next level and expressed honor at being part of his final matches, though he had pitched the team name "Phenomenal Dragons" under the belief they would continue longer together.

stories.title: Chelsea Green injury on WWE SmackDown
stories.tldr: Chelsea Green confirmed she suffered a broken orbital bone during her SmackDown match, requiring an emergency room visit. Medical guidelines suggest 6-8 weeks away from contact sports for uncomplicated orbital fractures. Green expressed frustration about the injury feeling "different" from past ones she's incorporated into her character, though she remained determined about her championship future.

stories.title: Brock Rechsteiler WWE signing reports
stories.tldr: WWE has expressed near-certain interest in signing Brock Rechsteiner once his NFL career ends, with one company higher-up putting the odds at "99.9 percent." The Steiner family prospect would bypass the traditional tryout process and be signed directly, and his current six-game suspension is not expected to affect WWE's plans.

stories.title: Nick Aldis WWE SmackDown GM role
stories.tldr: In a recent interview, Aldis revealed that his GM role allowed his body to properly heal from lingering back issues that had plagued him for years, including an inflamed muscle that was initially misdiagnosed. He also opened up about his regretful final TNA match against AJ Styles, calling it a "dubious honor" that was heavily overbooked and unfairly damaged his reputation at the time.

stories.title: WWE NXT main roster call-ups
stories.tldr: Following her SmackDown debut, Paxley posted emotional reactions on social media expressing her love for her new alliance with Bliss and Flair, while also sharing an Instagram photo gallery reflecting on her journey through WWE NXT before her call-up. Her former tag team partner Izzi Dame offered an in-character send-off mixed with genuine sentiment about missing working with Paxley.

stories.title: Rhea Ripley WWE injury and return timeline
stories.tldr: WWE has updated Rhea Ripley's return timeline to February 2027 Royal Rumble following her torn meniscus surgery. Chelsea Green, who won the interim title at SummerSlam, is now being promoted as the full WWE Women's Champion rather than an interim titleholder, suggesting WWE views her as Ripley's long-term replacement until the veteran's recovery is complete.

stories.title: WWE Royal Rumble 2027 two-night event
stories.tldr: WWE officially announced the 2027 Royal Rumble will take place at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona. While some internally advocated for making it a two-night event, the current plan keeps it as a one-night show, potentially the last before expansion. Dave Meltzer expressed caution about a women's Rumble drawing a strong stadium crowd on its own.

stories.title: Avery Styles controversy between AJ Styles and Arik Cannon
stories.tldr: Avery Styles faced criticism from veteran wrestler Arik Cannon for allegedly avoiding setup work at a GCW show in Minneapolis, prompting a heated social media exchange with his father AJ Styles. AJ argued his son was hired to wrestle, not work crew, and that any issues should be addressed privately rather than publicly. Lexis King later defended Avery, arguing that sons of famous wrestlers are treated differently by promoters and that veterans should mentor rather than embarrass young talent online.

stories.title: Multi-promotion injury report
stories.tldr: Multiple wrestling promotions are dealing with significant injuries across their rosters. Notable names sidelined include Bronson Reed with a distal bicep tear requiring surgery, Logan Paul facing six months recovery from a torn triceps, Rhea Ripley recovering from knee surgery, and various other talent dealing with injuries ranging from shoulder issues to neck problems with no confirmed return dates for most.

stories.title: Grand Slam 2 wrestling event
stories.tldr: Grand Slam 2 returns to Kokomo Municipal Stadium on August 15 with championship matches and hometown wrestler Chris Owens facing Jacob Brawn. The inaugural Grand Slam drew approximately 600 fans in August 2024, and positive audience feedback convinced organizers to bring the event back. The new show will start later to avoid excessive heat and aims to present accessible wrestling storytelling without requiring prior knowledge of wrestler histories.

stories.title: MVP retirement plans
stories.tldr: MVP has announced plans to wrestle his final match in 2027 before retiring permanently. The veteran wrestler cited declining physical capabilities and waning passion for in-ring competition as reasons for the timeline. While uninterested in pursuing singles championships, MVP remains open to tag team or trios matches with Bobby Lashley and Shelton Benjamin as part of The Hurt Syndicate.

stories.title: AAA TripleMania 34 WWE co-promotion matches
stories.tldr: WWE and AAA will co-promote TripleMania 34 across two nights in Las Vegas and Mexico City on September 11 and 13. The article outlines six potential matches that could be added to the card, including title matches for the Latin American Championship, Mixed Tag Team Championship, and WWE and AAA World Tag Team Championships, plus high-profile dream matches featuring WWE stars like Damian Priest, R-Truth, and Omos competing in the AAA promotion.

stories.title: CMLL International Grand Prix
stories.tldr: Hechicero won the CMLL International Grand Prix on August 7, 2026, an 11-on-11 torneo cibernetico pitting Mexico against the rest of the world. The Mexican wrestler defeated PAC and Claudio Castagnoli in the final sequence, continuing his heated rivalry with Castagnoli over the CMLL World Heavyweight Championship.

stories.title: Joe Gacy first championship post-WWE
stories.tldr: Joe Gacy, now performing under his real name Joseph Sawyer, has won his first championship since leaving WWE after a nearly six-year tenure. Sawyer defeated Anthony Gangone to capture the Xcite Wrestling Heavyweight Champion title on Friday night, marking a significant milestone in his post-WWE career on the independent wrestling circuit.

stories.title: Ricky Saints Teases AAA World Cruiserweight Title Chase After Confronting Rey Fenix
stories.tldr: Ricky Saints interrupted an interview with Rey Fenix to issue a direct challenge for the AAA World Cruiserweight Championship, signaling a shift in his focus away from main roster championship pursuits. After losing a U.S. Championship opportunity at Night of Champions in June, Saints appears ready to target Fenix's title that was most recently defended on SmackDown.

stories.title: Tony Khan Adds Last-Minute Match to AEW Collision After Stream Audio Cuts Out
stories.tldr: Tony Khan announced a last-minute addition to AEW Collision for August 8, booking The Brawling Birds against Viva Van and VertVixen in a tag team match during a Twitter stream. However, the stream's audio cut out immediately after the announcement, leaving uncertainty about whether Khan revealed any additional matches or card changes before the technical difficulty occurred.

stories.title: Dominik Mysterio AAA appearances and WWE booking
stories.tldr: Dominik Mysterio is reportedly frustrated with his comedic WWE RAW booking compared to his serious AAA Mega Champion role, feeling he's being treated as two separate characters on different shows. Meanwhile, CM Punk has teased a potential AAA appearance at the upcoming Worlds Collide event in Chicago, hinting he may return to wearing a mask for lucha libre fans.

stories.title: AAA Triplemanía 34 event
stories.tldr: Dominik Mysterio will defend the AAA Mega Championship against El Grande Americano at Triplemanía 34, with the match officially confirmed during Verano de Escándalo week three. Mysterio recently took shots at Americano during an interview, claiming he cannot be trusted and vowing to destroy him at the event.

stories.title: EC3 health concerns
stories.tldr: Despite Rockstar Spud's explanation that EC3 was selling injury, speculation about the wrestler's health continued online. EC3 responded Saturday with shirtless photos and a lengthy social media post about wellness and accountability, though he did not directly address the specific health concerns fans raised.

stories.title: Multiple Matches Revealed for August 12 AEW Dynamite
stories.tldr: AEW announced three additional matches for the August 12 Dynamite episode in Las Vegas. New Continental Cup first-round bouts were confirmed for Jay White vs. David Finlay and Jack Perry vs. Jon Moxley. A triple-threat match between Nick Wayne, MJF and Mike Bailey will determine who earns the No. 2 spot in the Casino Gauntlet at All In London.

stories.title: More WWE Main Roster Call Ups After Tatum Paxley
stories.tldr: Following Tatum Paxley's main roster debut, WWE has several other NXT stars positioned for call-ups to Raw or SmackDown. Candidates include Lola Vice (former NXT Women's Champion), the tag team of Hank Walker and Tank Ledger, Myles Borne (currently a double champion), and several others gaining momentum on the developmental brand.

stories.title: Jim Ross Brain Surgery and AEW Contract
stories.tldr: Jim Ross, the 74-year-old AEW senior commentator, is scheduled to undergo brain surgery on Wednesday, August 12, in Norman, Oklahoma, where doctors will insert a shunt to drain excess fluid from his brain. His AEW contract expires this month, and while Ross has not yet signed a new deal, he expressed willingness to accept if Tony Khan decides not to renew, emphasizing his hope for a planned ending to his broadcasting career rather than an abrupt departure.

stories.title: Claudio Castagnoli on Influencers in Wrestling
stories.tldr: AEW's Claudio Castagnoli defended the use of influencers and celebrities in professional wrestling, explaining that while they bring new audiences to the business, the core of wrestling must remain the priority. Both WWE and AEW have incorporated celebrities into their programming, though WWE has utilized more high-profile names like Jelly Roll and Travis Scott compared to AEW's recent celebrity appearances.

stories.title: Tommaso Ciampa AEW Grand Slam Mexico
stories.tldr: Tommaso Ciampa generated significant social media buzz at AEW Grand Slam: Mexico on August 5, though not for his in-ring performance. After losing a three-way match to Andrade El Idolo, Ciampa borrowed a female fan's phone at ringside and took an inappropriate photo inside his trunks, which quickly went viral across social media platforms.

stories.title: Joey Janela 20th Anniversary Event
stories.tldr: Joey Janela celebrated his 20th Anniversary Event on August 6, 2026, where he praised wrestler Megan Bayne as a top-five women's performer in the world. Following a mixed tag team match, Janela called on AEW President Tony Khan to allow Bayne to compete against male wrestlers on television, arguing that such opportunities would establish her as the best professional wrestler in the world.

stories.title: AEW Grand Slam Star Return
stories.tldr: Buddy Matthews issued a warning to the AEW roster upon receiving medical clearance, stating he carries "a lot of anger, a lot of rage" after 18 months away and vowing to show what the world missed. The landscape of AEW has shifted significantly during his absence, with his Hounds of Hell partner Brody King now thriving as part of the AEW World Trios Champions, while Malakai Black has departed the company and returned to his independent wrestling identity as Tommy End.

stories.title: Roman Reigns Survivor Series WarGames
stories.tldr: Roman Reigns, the current WWE World Heavyweight Champion, has been officially added to the promotional material for Survivor Series: WarGames 2026, which takes place on November 28 at Daikin Park in Houston, Texas. While his appearance on the poster confirms his presence at the event, WWE has not officially announced what role he will have, though his prominent placement suggests a significant involvement. This adds to his already busy schedule that includes Money in the Bank in October and a title defense in Mexico City in September.

stories.title: Bobby Steveson Lightning Strike
stories.tldr: Bobby Steveson, the former WWE NXT wrestler who performed under the ring name Damon Kemp, survived a lightning strike on Friday and posted a hospital photo confirming the incident. The 24-year-old competitive wrestler and country music artist did not provide details about where or how the strike occurred, but indicated the situation was serious enough to require medical hospitalization and treatment.

stories.title: Brock Lesnar vs Gunther Match Scrapped
stories.tldr: WWE had plans to book a dream match between Brock Lesnar and Gunther at WrestleMania on two separate occasions, but both fell through before fans could see the bout. The first attempt was scrapped before creative details were revealed, while the second plan was derailed after Lesnar was implicated in a lawsuit filed by former WWE employee Janel Grant in early 2024. Despite Lesnar's recent retirement announcement following his loss to Oba Femi at SummerSlam, the match remains a viable option should Lesnar decide to return.

stories.title: Kevin Owens CM Punk Feud
stories.tldr: Kevin Owens won a number one contender's match at SummerSlam and has requested his WWE Championship match against CM Punk take place on August 21, 2026 in Toronto, Canada. This comes as CM Punk acknowledged his SummerSlam victory over Cody Rhodes was controversial due to Randy Orton's interference, and has offered Rhodes a rematch anytime he wants one. The championship picture is heating up with multiple contenders vying for title opportunities.

stories.title: WWE Undertaker Interview
stories.tldr: The Undertaker recently opened up about his storied wrestling career, revealing that he preferred working with Stone Cold Steve Austin at live events due to the creative freedom available there, and explaining how Triple H's encouragement before WrestleMania 31 helped him overcome serious self-doubt following a severe concussion that ended his undefeated WrestleMania streak the year prior.

stories.title: Bully Ray Comments on WWE Angles
stories.tldr: Bully Ray praised WWE's handling of Oba Femi's main roster push, highlighting both a meaningful backstage moment at SummerSlam where Femi thanked Brock Lesnar for passing the torch, and an on-air angle on Raw that set up intriguing storylines involving Femi, Bron Breakker, and Paul Heyman. Ray believes the creative setup has established mutual respect between Femi and Heyman, tension between Breakker and Heyman, and a compelling face-to-face confrontation between Femi and Breakker that could elevate Breakker's position.

stories.title: Matt Hardy Vince McMahon WWE Producer Discussion
stories.tldr: Matt Hardy revealed that Vince McMahon pushed him to transition into a full-time producer or coaching role near the end of his 2020 WWE contract, but Hardy declined because he wanted to continue wrestling while his body allowed. Hardy believed McMahon saw greater financial potential in other wrestlers like Jeff Hardy, Edge, and Christian, and predicted that even if he briefly pursued an in-ring storyline, McMahon would have eventually moved him into a backstage position, which ultimately influenced his decision to leave WWE.

stories.title: Shinsuke Nakamura SmackDown Return
stories.tldr: Shinsuke Nakamura made his WWE SmackDown return on the August 7 episode via a video message, announcing he will challenge The Mighty Fortunes (The MFTs) but will not fight alone this time. The King of Strong Style teased that an unnamed ally will join him in his war against the group, which has used superior numbers to their advantage in their ongoing rivalry. Nakamura's mysterious partner remains unannounced, leaving fans speculating about who will stand beside him.

stories.title: Potential Zilla Fatu WWE Debut
stories.tldr: Zilla Fatu, son of late WWE star Umaga and cousin to multiple current WWE Bloodline members, has departed House of Glory after losing his HOG Crown Jewel Championship to Amazing Red. The announcers indicated Fatu is moving on to bigger opportunities, and he was previously spotted at the WWE Performance Center in June, suggesting an impending WWE debut.

stories.title: Carlito WWE Departure Comments
stories.tldr: Carlito has departed WWE and revealed he is now open to opportunities elsewhere after achieving his retirement goal with the company. In a recent interview, he compared staying loyal to WWE to "being a beaten housewife," expressing frustration with how he was treated despite his loyalty to the organization over the years.

stories.title: WWE Hall of Fame 2027 Tag Teams
stories.tldr: As WWE prepares for WrestleMania 43 weekend in Saudi Arabia in 2027, the company is considering which legendary tag teams to induct into the Hall of Fame that year. The article lists seven potential inductees ranging from Attitude Era teams like The Headbangers to modern-day legends like The Usos and The New Day, each bringing significant accomplishments and historical significance to WWE's tag team division.

stories.title: WWE Star NXT Experience Reflection
stories.tldr: Finn Balor reflected on his early WWE career in NXT, initially believing he was wasting his prime years training in Florida after competing at the Tokyo Dome. Performance Center coach Terry Taylor convinced him that learning WWE's distinct wrestling style would extend his career by over a decade, advice that Balor credits with keeping him healthy and relevant 12 years later.

stories.title: WWE SmackDown Start Time August 6
stories.tldr: WWE SmackDown is scheduled for tonight from the Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, PA, with the broadcast beginning at 8pm Eastern time on Friday, August 7, 2026. The article provides comprehensive global start times for viewers across multiple regions and time zones to help international audiences tune in at the appropriate time for their location.

stories.title: WWE SmackDown 8/7/2026 Coverage
stories.tldr: Kevin Owens and CM Punk engaged in a heated verbal confrontation on the 8/7 SmackDown, with Owens blasting the champion over his perceived arrogance and calling him a "miserable piece of shit." Cody Rhodes escalated his feud with Randy Orton by declaring he no longer has to be the good guy and challenging Orton as "the last legend left" in WWE. Multiple title matches were set for the 8/14 Boston show, and Shinsuke Nakamura teased a return with a mysterious tag team partner to go to war with the MFT.

stories.title: Chelsea Green Women's Championship
stories.tldr: WWE presented Green simply as "Women's Champion" rather than "Interim Women's Champion" on the August 7 SmackDown, with Green wearing a shirt reading "Permanent Champion," suggesting the company may officially upgrade her status soon. However, Green's celebration was cut short when Fatal Influence defeated her and Tiffany Stratton in an impromptu tag team title match, with Nia Jax and Lash Legend attacking both women afterward and standing over Green with her title.

stories.title: Tatum Paxley Main Roster Debut
stories.tldr: Tatum Paxley made her main roster debut on the August 7 SmackDown, appearing during the Charlotte Flair vs. Jade Cargill main event alongside a returning Alexa Bliss. Paxley helped Flair secure victory over Cargill and the two celebrated together in the ring, suggesting WWE may be building a new trio on the blue brand. Charlotte Flair reportedly requested Paxley be brought to SmackDown, and Paxley has cited Bliss as a long-time inspiration.

stories.title: Roman Reigns Mexico City Tournament
stories.tldr: WWE has officially unveiled the complete eight-man tournament bracket to determine Roman Reigns' challenger for Mexico City on September 14, with first-round matches beginning August 10. The bracket creates the possibility of a finals matchup between real-life brothers Penta and Rey Fenix, which would mark their first WWE singles encounter. Notably absent from the tournament are El Grande Americano—who was previously rumored as Reigns' opponent—and Dominik Mysterio.

stories.title: WWE Shareholder Lawsuit Settlement
stories.tldr: Court filings have revealed McMahon will pay $42.5 million as part of the $147.5 million total settlement, with TKO contributing $105 million. Shareholders accused TKO of making incomplete disclosures that misrepresented the full payout. The settlement finalization is now stalled over a dispute between McMahon and other co-defendants regarding their insurance indemnification agreements.

stories.title: Nick Aldis WWE SummerSlam Return
stories.tldr: Nick Aldis faced Gunther at SummerSlam 2026 after nearly three years away from in-ring competition, delivering an impressive performance despite losing the match. WWE currently has no creative plans for him to wrestle again, though the door remains open for a potential future match. Aldis said he didn't lobby for the opportunity but was always prepared to step back in the ring.

stories.title: WWE SummerSlam 2026 Post-Event News
stories.tldr: Corbin retained his US title against Trick Williams on SmackDown using the same underhanded tactics that won him the championship at SummerSlam, hitting Williams with the belt while the referee was distracted. Meanwhile, SummerSlam 2026 drew disappointing attendance figures of around 35,000 per night after heavy discounting and papering, prompting WWE to withhold the official number—a particularly sore subject as AEW's All In London is already outpacing the gate.

stories.title: Netflix Dominik Mysterio Edit Controversy
stories.tldr: Both Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch have responded to Netflix's removal of the controversial line, with Morgan joking about it on social media and Lynch appearing amused rather than upset. Most significantly, the line was reportedly scripted and pre-approved by WWE leadership, including Triple H, raising questions about why it was edited out despite that approval.

stories.title: Becky Lynch WWE Return
stories.tldr: Lynch and Balor announced WWE Raw will broadcast live from Dublin's 3Arena on January 25, 2027, marking the first time the red brand has ever aired from Ireland. The show will be available live on Netflix globally. Lynch also discussed her current role elevating younger talent and revealed she and husband Seth Rollins spend hours discussing WWE creative together.

stories.title: Ryback Defends Roman Reigns
stories.tldr: Ryback defended Roman Reigns on social media, pushing back against Conrad Thompson's claim that Reigns is overrated. Ryback argued that while Reigns received company backing early in his career, what matters is what he did with those opportunities, and that wrestling benefits from recognizing achievement rather than tearing people down.

stories.title: Shiloh Hill NXT Injury Update
stories.tldr: Shiloh Hill made his injury public via video message on NXT, revealing the specific nature of his fractured maxilla and sharing his optimistic outlook on a potential early return. Hill promoted upcoming NXT Live events in Melbourne and Jacksonville while emphasizing he remains focused on his recovery timeline.

stories.title: Big Cass WWE Return
stories.tldr: Big Cass has reconnected with numerous WWE talents backstage since his return, indicating a positive reception to his comeback. He's entering this second run with improved mindset and purpose compared to his first tenure, though he never won championships during his original stint with the company.

stories.title: Rhea Ripley Injury Status
stories.tldr: WWE is now targeting the Royal Rumble in January for Rhea Ripley's return from knee surgery, meaning she could miss the remainder of 2024. Chelsea Green won the interim title at SummerSlam and may be awarded the official championship, with WWE's decision on the title status still pending. Ripley confirmed on social media that surgery was necessary due to the severity of her meniscus tear.

stories.title: WWE Star Television Debut Concerns
stories.tldr: During a recent interview, Becky Lynch reflected on her embarrassing NXT debut in 2014, where she performed an Irish dance stereotype that she now views as "the world's worst" debut in wrestling history—worse even than the infamous Shockmaster incident. Lynch emphasized that unlike Shockmaster's unintentional fall, her terrible debut was completely intentional, making it arguably more cringe-worthy in her own assessment.

stories.title: AAA on Fox Dominik Mysterio
stories.tldr: Dominik Mysterio will appear in an exclusive interview segment on AAA on Fox this Saturday, August 8, as part of the ongoing Verano de Escandalo storyline involving his betrayal of El Grande Americano. WWE and AAA have also announced a major doubleheader event on August 30 in Texas, with AAA's "Ola De Calor" show featuring Dominik defending his Mega Championship against El Grande Americano (Ludwig Kaiser), followed by NXT Heatwave later that same day.

stories.title: Wrestling Observer Podcast Episodes
stories.tldr: Wrestling Observer Live returned with an absinthe-themed Fun Friday episode featuring Bryan Alvarez, Lance Storm, and Filthy Tom Lawlor discussing news and taking listener calls. Meanwhile, Wrestling Weekly covered major WWE developments from SummerSlam including Brock Lesnar's retirement and Roman Reigns' status, while also discussing AEW's upcoming Wembley Stadium show and MJF's return to action.

stories.title: Lady Frost Cancer-Free Update
stories.tldr: Lady Frost, a former AEW and ROH wrestler currently signed to MLW, announced on Thursday that she is cancer-free following a recent health scare. The wrestler encouraged women to get regular mammogram screenings and expressed her readiness to return to in-ring competition, with a triple threat match scheduled for this Saturday on MLW Fusion.

stories.title: BRCW Summer Smash Card
stories.tldr: Boca Raton Championship Wrestling has updated its Summer Smash card for August 16, 2026, with the biggest change being the main event. The vacant BRCW Championship will now be decided in a Fatal Four-Way Match featuring Matt Riddle, Stallion Rogers, "Main Event Monster" Fulton, and Matt Taven, after Steve Maclin's indefinite suspension vacated the title. This change has ripple effects throughout the card, including adjustments to the tag team division.

stories.title: AAA Verano de Escándalo
stories.tldr: AAA has announced a Latin American Title qualifier for the final week of Verano de Escándalo on August 8th, featuring El Fiscal, Psycho Clown, and Cruz Del Toro competing in a three-way match. The winner will join La Parka and El Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr. in a four-way match at Triplemanía 34, with one additional qualifier still to be determined from an Omos vs. Damian Priest vs. Galeno match.

stories.title: TNA Free Agent Championship Strip
stories.tldr: Steve Maclin has been stripped of the Boca Raton Championship Wrestling Heavyweight Championship following a virtual confrontation with promotion officials. The championship removal appears to be a worked angle to explain his departure amid widespread speculation that he will sign with either AEW or WWE. Maclin's wife Deonna Purrazzo currently works for AEW, and he previously wrestled in WWE as Steve Cutler from 2014 to 2020.

stories.title: Ted Arcidi Wrestling History Comments
stories.tldr: Ted Arcidi, the original "World's Strongest Man" in WWE, discussed his remarkable recovery from five joint replacement surgeries performed simultaneously, crediting strict physical therapy and discipline for returning to near peak strength levels. The legendary strongman also reflected on his entry into professional wrestling through Ken Patera's connection to Vince McMahon and shared insights about WWE's golden era dominance in the 1980s.

stories.title: Ask Tito Column
stories.tldr: In this edition of "Ask Tito," the columnist responds to criticism that Roman Reigns is "overrated" and an "industry plant" by arguing that while he was "shoved down our throats" in the 2010s, his heel turn with Paul Heyman and the Bloodline storyline from 2021-2024 made him genuinely effective. The column contends that Roman remains WWE's top draw despite losing momentum after WrestleMania 40, and that a missed Rock vs. Roman feud could have elevated him further. The piece also critiques Conrad Thompson's podcast influence and the excessive interjection of producer opinions in wrestling podcasts.

stories.title: TNA Hardcore Justice 2011 Flashback
stories.tldr: Winter defeated Mickie James for the TNA Knockouts Championship at TNA Hardcore Justice 2011 on August 7, earning a rare negative one star rating from Dave Meltzer. The match was marred by poor coordination between the wrestlers, constant interference from Angelina Love that killed the crowd heat, and several botched spots that left the performers clearly out of sync with each other.

stories.title: Matt Hardy TNA World Championship Advertising
stories.tldr: Matt Hardy defended TNA's advertising of the Jeff Hardy vs. Nic Nemeth TNA World Championship match, which was taped on July 30 in Philadelphia but did not air on the live Impact broadcast that night. Hardy argued the company did not falsely advertise the match for the live show, noting that the graphic never explicitly stated it would air live and that information about which matches were airing live was available on the website and social media. While acknowledging casual fans may have been confused, Hardy emphasized that reading comprehension was important and that the ads were primarily designed to sell tickets for the Philadelphia taping.

stories.title: Fatal Influence Pin Chelsea Green, Retain WWE Women's Tag Titles On SmackDown
stories.tldr: Fatal Influence retained their WWE Women's Tag Team Championships by defeating interim Women's Champion Chelsea Green and Women's US Champion Tiffany Stratton on SmackDown. The match was made impromptu after Fatal Influence interrupted Green's celebration and Stratton agreed to challenge Jayne for the US title next week if the tag titles were on the line. After winning via the Fatal Flaw finisher, Fatal Influence and the champions were attacked by the Irresistible Forces, with Nia Jax taking Green's interim title.

stories.title: Roman Reigns WWE WrestleMania 43 Opponent
stories.tldr: With WrestleMania 43 scheduled for April 2027 in Saudi Arabia, Roman Reigns is expected to be in a high-profile main event match as the current World Heavyweight Champion. The article lists eight potential opponents including CM Punk, Drew McIntyre, Bron Breakker, Jacob Fatu, GUNTHER, and Cody Rhodes, each with their own storyline justification for facing The OTC.

stories.title: Nattie Calls For WWE Hall Of Fame Legend To Come Out Of Retirement, Proposes Scenario For Comeback Match
stories.tldr: Natalya suggested that WWE Hall of Famer AJ Styles could be convinced to come out of retirement for a father-son tag team match with his son Avery Styles after witnessing Avery's impressive performance at a GCW event during SummerSlam week. Nattie praised both Avery's natural in-ring presence and his professional demeanor, highlighting that he is earning his opportunities through hard work rather than relying on his famous last name.

stories.title: CM Punk Cuts Promo At WWE Fairfax Live Event Addressing “What Went Down At SummerSlam” & Makes Promise
stories.tldr: CM Punk addressed his controversial SummerSlam victory over Cody Rhodes at a WWE live event in Fairfax, Virginia, acknowledging that he won the match in a "dirty" fashion after Randy Orton's surprise interference. Despite being the Undisputed WWE Champion with Kevin Owens lined up as his next challenger, Punk promised Rhodes an immediate rematch whenever he wants it, emphasizing their friendship and respect.

stories.title: Dory Funk Jr. Legacy and Tributes
stories.tldr: CM Punk honored Dory Funk Jr. during a WWE live event in Fairfax, Virginia on Thursday by using the spinning toe hold, Funk's signature submission, instead of pinning his opponent after hitting a Go To Sleep. The tribute comes days after Punk also paid homage to Dory's brother Terry Funk at SummerSlam. Wrestling Observer Radio and the Pacific Rim podcast have also devoted coverage to Funk's lasting influence on professional wrestling globally, particularly in Japan where he trained future legends.

stories.title: TNA Knockouts Division Updates
stories.tldr: TNA is rebuilding its Knockouts division following multiple recent departures including Jody Threat, Mara Sade, Tessa Blanchard, and others. The promotion has already signed Gabby Forza and is actively recruiting additional women's talent. Additionally, a former TNA Knockouts champion is set to return to the division.

stories.title: Aleister Black Post-WWE Update
stories.tldr: Tommy End, formerly known as Aleister Black, has released a cryptic "day in the life" video on Instagram following his WWE release, showing his transition back to his original ring name and martial arts training. The video contrasts his mundane daily routine with intense combat preparation, reflecting what he describes as the duality of his next chapter in wrestling.

stories.title: Undertaker AAA Creative Vision
stories.tldr: Undertaker has detailed his creative philosophy for AAA, emphasizing storytelling, athleticism, and aggression as the cornerstones of his vision. He's pushing talent to embrace edgier, more violent performances and positioning AAA as distinctly different from WWE's other brands. The roster is increasingly buying into his direction and the wrestling community is taking notice.

stories.title: Brock Rechsteiner NFL Suspension
stories.tldr: The NFL has not yet disclosed the reason for Brock Rechsteiner's six-game suspension to begin his career with the New Orleans Saints. The suspension will take effect after the Saints reduce their roster to 53 players on August 30th, though he remains eligible for training camp and preseason competition.

stories.title: Backstage WWE News: Another Big Behind-The-Scenes Departure, Women’s Title Rumors, Big Cass Update, Netflix/Raw Edit Note
stories.tldr: Beyond Patrick Dooley's departure, new reports indicate Rhea Ripley faces months of recovery from surgery, with Chelsea Green expected to be recognized as the official Undisputed WWE Women's Champion. Additionally, Netflix removed a controversial line from Becky Lynch's segment with Liv Morgan, though the remark was planned in advance rather than improvised.

stories.title: Former NXT Women's Champion Reportedly Backstage At WWE SmackDown
stories.tldr: Tatum Paxley is confirmed backstage at Friday's SmackDown in Philadelphia, suggesting her main roster debut is imminent. Fellow NXT star Lola Vice, who appeared to say goodbye to the Performance Center crowd after losing the NXT Underground match this week, is also rumored for a SmackDown debut, though her presence at the event is unconfirmed.

stories.title: Multiple Returns Set For Post-SummerSlam Episode Of WWE SmackDown On August 7
stories.tldr: Randy Orton has also returned at SummerSlam and will appear on tonight's SmackDown, where he delivered a match-changing RKO to Cody Rhodes during the CM Punk vs. Rhodes title match. CM Punk is also confirmed for the show, along with new Interim Women's Champion Chelsea Green making an appearance. A special ticket discount is available with code LASTCHANCE.

stories.title: WWE SmackDown venue advertising Randy Orton, discounted tickets for tonight’s show
stories.tldr: While Randy Orton wasn't listed on WWE's official SmackDown preview, the Philadelphia venue is heavily promoting his return for tonight's show and offering discounted tickets to drive ticket sales. The arena has moved multiple promotional offers this week, including 30% off with a last-chance code expiring Friday morning, following an earlier two-for-one ticket package. Current ticket distribution stands at 9,138 for tonight's event.
